title: Fractional-merge admission controller and attention-phase pacing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: p99 tail latency spikes for mixed short/long sequence workloads during sustained microbursts. Existing admission logic waits for full-window batching which causes long waits for short requests or causes large batches that force fallback kernels and KV cache thrashing. Goal: implement a fractional-merge admission controller that allows controlled partial batch coalescing across micro-windows, and an attention-phase pacing layer that pre-schedules KV prewarm and kernel hints based on early token distribution. The controller should reduce p99 by 15-25% for targeted workloads while keeping cost within current budget. Work includes algorithm design, kernel-hint integration, metrics and canary rollout in staging and a limited production cohort.
acceptance_criteria: p99 end-to-end latency for mixed short/long sequences decreases by >=15% on benchmark harness (see Grafana dashboard)
No regression (>5%) in median latency or throughput for heavy long-sequence batches
Kernel-selection hints are emitted and consumed by runtime (validated in canary) with <1% error rate
Canary rollout demonstrates stable memory/KV hitrate and no OOM events across 48h
Feature flag + rollout plan and docs updated; one on-call runbook entry added for new admission metrics
tasks: Design fractional-merge algorithm and credit model (prototype in Rust)
Add attention-phase estimator: early-token analyzer for sequence-length and attention footprint
Integrate kernel-hint API between admission controller and kernel selection layer
Expose metrics: fractional_batch_ratio, prewarm_savings_ms, kv_prewarm_hit, kernel_hint_mismatch
Create canary config: 10% traffic on staging -> 5% production cohort with rollback policy
Prepare rollout runbook and add Grafana/Alert thresholds
